title: A Damselfly Peeking Through a Leaf Wins Big Photo Prize
summary:
Have you ever seen a bug peeking through a leaf? That's exactly what won the 2026 BMC Ecology and Evolution and BMC Zoology image competition! The winning photo shows an orange-tailed marsh dart damselfly—a tiny, colorful insect—looking right through a hole in a leaf. A student named Sritam Kumar Sethy took the picture in a wetland in India. The judges loved it because the damselfly seems to have a real personality, like it's saying hello!

Damselflies are super important. They live both in water and on land, so if a wetland is polluted or damaged, they're some of the first creatures to disappear. That makes them like nature's health inspectors. The photo reminds us that wetlands are amazing homes for all kinds of life, but they're also in danger from pollution and climate change.

The contest had lots of other cool winners too. One photo shows two students in Oregon attaching a tiny radio transmitter to a red-legged frog at night. The transmitter helps scientists track where the frog goes, so they can protect its habitat. Another picture captures two giant Australian cuttlefish fighting for a female's attention—they change their skin color to show off! There's also a photo of noisy friarbirds teaming up to chase away a hawk, and a heartwarming shot of a baby sea turtle being helped to the ocean by people who protected its nest.

All these photos show how scientists work hard to understand and protect animals. They also remind us that nature is full of surprises—sometimes right in front of our eyes, peeking through a leaf!
why_it_matters: Next time you see a bug near a puddle or park pond, you can think about how it might be a tiny signal about whether that water is healthy.
